shock.title: Three food-price spikes since 2007, each peak higher than the last
shock.subtitle: FAO Food Price Index, all foods, monthly. Peaks: 132.7 → 137.7 → 160.2. The Mar 2022 peak is the highest since the index began in 1990.
legend: Shock month: prices more than 20% above a year earlier
shock.source: **Source:** FAO Food Price Index (2014–16 = 100), Jan 1990 to Mar 2026. Shock months computed from year-on-year change.
shock.takeaway: Each shock lasted more than a year. Prices are still 128.5 today, well above the 2014–16 base of 100.

exposure.title: 20 of 91 countries pair serious hunger with high food-import reliance
exposure.subtitle: Each dot is a country. These countries buy much of their food abroad, so a global price spike lands on households that are already hungry.
legend: Exposed: serious hunger and above-median food imports
exposure.source: **Sources:** Global Hunger Index 2025; World Bank, food imports (% of merchandise imports), latest year 2015–2024 per country. **Note:** labels name some of the 20 exposed countries.
exposure.takeaway: These 20 countries are the first places to watch and prepare when a shock signal appears.

warning.title: Oils and cereals rose 20% before every food-price shock since 2000
warning.subtitle: The two-price signal fired 5 times. 4 were followed by a shock 1 to 5 months later; one (2002) was not.
legend: Signal: oils and cereals both 20%+ above a year earlier, with months until the shock
warning.source: **Source:** FAO Food Price Index, monthly, Jan 2000 to Mar 2026. **Note:** the rule was read off this same history, so it is a signal to watch, not a tested forecast.
warning.takeaway: No signal now. In Mar 2026 oils are +13% and cereals +1% on a year earlier.
